recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13320 unless a future work-group decision changes token or logical-id search semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-13320 was a Published FHIR-core search issue resolved as Persuasive. It asked for clarification that all _id searches are case-sensitive, token search case sensitivity depends on the underlying data semantics, exact-match wording should not imply generic case-insensitive token behavior, Resource-level search parameters should appear in the search summary table, token searches over string data are not case-sensitive, and the token safety tradeoff should be documented.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 2d2371c75b043e4332188b63d93cdc5fc7667767, '#13320 notes about case sensitivity on token searches', with git-svn revision 12779 matching the Jira application comment. That patch added the _id always-case-sensitive note, refined token exact-match wording, added context-dependent token case-sensitivity language, added the string-backed-token note, and added the safety note.
additional_context: source/search.html is in the current publication set through publish.ini. Current search.html still says token matches are literal and case-sensitive unless context indicates otherwise, _id matches are always case-sensitive, and string-backed token searches are not case-sensitive. The dedicated _id section explains code-only token matching rather than case-insensitive string starts-with behavior, and the summary table includes the Resource-level _id row. The later 2022 search refactor preserved these semantics, and related FHIR-6123, FHIR-13655, and FHIR-19673 audit commits are already present on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The authoritative current source already satisfies the Jira resolution, so adding redundant prose would not change implementer understanding.
